description: The authors developed and validated a dynamic rainfall-runoff simulation linked to water quality for 35 combined-sewer spillways in the Rio Vallescura catchment, central Italy. The model identifies critical flow and pollutant discharges and compares treatment or management scenarios. Source results include suspended solids, oxygen-demand indicators, nitrogen and Escherichia coli; disinfection experiments supplement the modelling. The abstract reports E. coli load reductions of 28–73 percent in the body while its highlight says up to 74 percent. This small source discrepancy is preserved without selecting a preferred value. Code, calibration inputs and application beyond the studied catchment remain unverified. The source documents a water quality treatment or recovery study. The source authors provide this description through Zenodo, whose deposit declares CC BY 4.0 and public document access. Geographic and temporal coverage remain limited to the cases or observations explicitly described. Only metadata and file descriptors were reviewed; no document, measurements, model archive or code was read. Related components retain their source identities and uncertain experimental overlap. Document access and licensing do not establish executable availability or software rights.
